subject: Re: ZenPath – Data Processing Addendum, audit evidence & signing timeline

Subject: Data Processing Addendum (ZenPath redlines) + audit evidence request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Attached are the redlines from our legal team for the DPA we discussed. A few asks we want to confirm up front:

- Confirmation that Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and a summary of the latest penetration test findings (redacted is fine).
- Audit rights: ZenPath requires the ability to perform an annual compliance review (either on-site or via a third-party auditor) with 30 days' notice. We can accept reasonable confidentiality constraints.
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day notice for new subprocessors and an opportunity to object for critical data classes.
- Cross-border transfers: we prefer SCCs or equivalent mechanisms for international data flows.

Attached: ZenPath_DPA_Redline_20261110.docx

Please confirm whether you can provide the SOC2 report and a redacted pen test summary. Our procurement team would like to start DocuSign routing this week if possible — I can prepare our signing envelope once we agree on the audit clause language.

Best,
Olivia Grant
Director, Legal & Contracts
ZenPath Health

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data Processing Addendum (ZenPath redlines) + audit evidence request

Hi Olivia — thanks for sharing and for the clear list. I've looped in Dev (legal ops) and Marcus (security) to review the redlines and the audit request. Quick notes from our side:

- We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a summarized pen test report. Marcus will confirm acceptable redaction level.
- Audit rights: Redwood generally supports third-party audits or examinations by mutually agreed auditors. On-site audits are possible for enterprise contracts but we typically require limited scope, reasonable notice (30 days is fine in principle), and pre-agreed confidentiality protections.
- Subprocessor notification: we operate a public subprocessors registry and provide 30 days' notice for changes; objections are evaluated case-by-case.
- Cross-border transfers: we support SCCs and equivalent safeguards.

Dev — can you take the redline and propose language that narrows audit rights to either (a) Redwood-led independent attestation (SOC2 or equivalent) or (b) customer-engaged third-party assessment with a mutually agreed scope? If ZenPath insists on unbounded on-site access we should escalate.

Olivia — hoping to get this wrapped up quickly. If we can align on audit language today, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope and do parallel routing. Proposed timeline: legal redline by EOD; signatures by 2026-11-20.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood proposed revisions to ZenPath DPA (attached)

Hi Olivia — attached is our redline reflecting the items we discussed. Key points: 

1) Audit rights — revised to: customer may request a third-party assessment of Redwood's controls, limited to scope reasonably necessary to verify customer data handling. Assessment must be performed by an accredited auditor, with no direct access to production systems; any on-site review limited to facilities-level checks and done only where absolutely required with 45 days' notice.

2) Subprocessors — we will provide 30 days' notice of material changes and maintain a public registry; for requests to restrict a specific subprocessor we propose a formal review and, where appropriate, mitigation or substitution.

3) International transfers — we will provide SCCs where applicable and will work with customers on additional contractual safeguards if needed.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_zenpath_redline.docx

Also linking a draft DocuSign envelope for execution from our side: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d-zenpath (internal routing).

Marcus — can you confirm if the redacted SOC2 and pen test summary are ready to share? If so, I'll attach them to the envelope.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
[attachment: Redwood_DPA_zenpath_redline.docx]

From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@zenpath.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed revisions to ZenPath DPA (attached)

Thanks Dev — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups from ZenPath legal: 

- The proposed restriction on on-site access is noted, but ZenPath needs an explicit option for an annual on-site review for systems that process highly sensitive PHI-derived datasets. We can accept a narrow scope and confidentiality protocol, but it must remain an available remedy.
- For the third-party assessment, we need assurance that the auditor can obtain artifacts (logs, configuration snapshots) relevant to the agreed scope.

We are prepared to proceed with DocuSign if Redwood can: (a) provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report, (b) provide a redacted pen test executive summary, and (c) accept language that preserves a limited annual on-site option for high-risk datasets.

I will attach our signing envelope from ZenPath once we have an agreed clause set: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/zenpath-xyz-456

Regards,
Olivia

Subject: Final: DPA language and evidence handoff for execution

Hi Olivia — quick update after internal alignment with security and legal. We are willing to accept a narrowly scoped annual on-site review for high-risk datasets under the following constraints (we've drafted exact language in the attached redline):

- On-site reviews limited to pre-agreed checklist (control families and evidence types) and must be performed by an accredited third-party auditor.
- Redwood must receive at least 45 days' notice for any on-site review.
- Auditor access excludes privileged production accounts; evidence exchange will use secure file transfer with strict NDA protections.

Marcus has approved sharing the following artifacts in advance (redacted where required): SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2026_redacted.pdf and PenTest_Summary_2026_redacted.txt. Those are attached; please confirm receipt.

Once you confirm the attached redline language we will route the DocuSign envelope from our side and can complete signatures by 2026-11-20 as proposed. If you'd prefer to send ZenPath's envelope, confirm the link and signatories and we'll coordinate parallel routing.

Next steps:
- Olivia: confirm redline and whether ZenPath will accept our 45-day notice window for on-site reviews (or propose alternate timeline).
- Dev: prepare final DocuSign envelope if Olivia confirms.

Thanks everyone — want to get this across the finish line this week.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
